title: Map Dedicated tiers to standard hardware shapes + propose list pricing and discount guardrails (v1)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
Goal: finalize a v1 mapping from Dedicated tiers (Standard / Plus / Premium) to a small set of standardized hardware “shapes” per region, with list pricing guidance and discount guardrails that preserve margin targets and are simple enough for Sales Ops/Deal Desk.

Why now: we can’t publish/commit a throughput SLO without tying entitlements to concrete capacity units. Today quoting is bespoke (GPU count + “expected TPS”), which creates mismatched expectations, messy escalation, and inconsistent unit economics.

Deliverables (this ticket):
1) Tier → eligible shapes matrix by region (what Sales can quote, with allowed upgrades/downgrades)
2) List price (monthly) for each tier/shape combination with required term lengths, plus adders (extra replicas, extra regions)
3) Discount guardrails (self-serve vs sales-assisted; who can approve what) + deal desk triggers
4) Written assumptions (utilization targets, headroom, burst reserve, support cost allocation) + sensitivity notes
5) Hand-off to Sales Enablement for the Dedicated tier cheat sheet + quoting playbook

Non-goals:
- Not rewriting the full Dedicated MSA language (covered in PM-503)
- Not changing the core tier entitlements (covered in PM-489)
- Not producing the final SKU catalog in billing (follow-up once v1 is approved)

Inputs we will use:
- Shape catalog + perf profiles (Infra/Fleet)
- Dedicated unit economics model (FP&A)
- Tier entitlement draft (Product)
- Early customer willingness-to-pay signals (Sales calls, CRM notes)

Working principle: keep the public catalog small. Prefer 2–3 shapes per region max. Exceptions must be explicit and require VP approval so the fleet remains manageable.
acceptance_criteria: A single table exists that maps Standard/Plus/Premium to eligible shapes per region (US-East, US-West, EU-Central initially), with an explicit “default” per tier
List pricing (USD/month) is defined for each tier+shape with: minimum term, included burst policy assumptions, and what is/isn’t included (e.g., extra replicas)
Discount guardrails are documented as: max discretionary discount by tier, approval matrix, and deal desk triggers; includes floors that align to gross margin targets
Finance (Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra) signs off that pricing meets margin constraints under stated utilization/headroom assumptions
Sales Ops (Isabelle Laurent) confirms the guardrails are operationalizable in quoting
Links added to the pricing/packaging Confluence doc + Sales enablement cheat sheet draft
proposed_v1_mapping_notes:
Draft (subject to shape catalog confirmation):

Standard tier (cost-efficient, best-effort failover posture):
- Default shapes: L40S-4x (where available) or A100-2x equivalent
- Use cases: steady workloads with predictable context lengths; customers willing to pin model/version to maintain predictable perf

Plus tier (balanced + defined burst behavior):
- Default shapes: A100-4x or H100-2x (region-dependent supply)
- Use cases: mixed prompt lengths, higher variance, needs clearer burst rules + better support response

Premium tier (highest guarantees + reserved headroom / HA options):
- Default shapes: H100-4x (preferred) or A100-8x (fallback where H100 constrained)
- Use cases: latency/throughput sensitive, contractual commitments, stronger failover posture and fastest escalation

Important: throughput SLO is expressed as a floor tied to the shape and a supported model set, not a universal “tokens/sec” promise independent of model/version/context. Pricing must reflect that we’re guaranteeing capacity and prioritization, not a fixed output rate for arbitrary prompts.
pricing_assumptions_v1:
Draft assumptions to validate with FP&A:
- Target blended gross margin (Dedicated): Standard 50–55%, Plus 55–60%, Premium 60%+ (Premium includes more headroom but higher WTP)
- Utilization targets (committed capacity): Standard 65–70%, Plus 60–65%, Premium 55–60%
- Headroom / spare policy: aligns with tier capacity model (Premium reserves more to protect the floor + faster recovery)
- Burst reserve: priced implicitly (Plus/Premium) and metered for overages; Standard burst is best-effort and may throttle under contention
- Support cost allocation: Premium includes higher-touch support and faster response targets; bake into list price rather than “support add-on” in v1
- Region multipliers: account for GPU supply and colocation cost differences; maintain consistent discount floors across regions where possible to avoid arbitrage
discount_guardrails_draft:
Draft guardrails (to be finalized with Sales Ops + Deal Desk):
- Standard: up to 20% discretionary discount with Sales leadership approval; >20% requires Deal Desk + Finance sign-off
- Plus: up to 15% discretionary discount; >15% requires Deal Desk + Finance sign-off
- Premium: up to 10% discretionary discount; >10% requires VP Sales + Finance sign-off

Deal Desk triggers (any tier):
- Non-standard shapes / custom hardware requests
- Multi-region HA promises or contractual failover language beyond tier standard
- Term < 12 months or ramp with large early headroom requirements
- Any pricing that falls below the published GM floor under stated utilization assumptions

Notes:
- We should define “GM floor” per shape and publish internally as a quoting calculator output (don’t put the number in customer-facing docs).
- Any “tokens/sec guarantee” language must be routed back to PM-503; pricing guidance should avoid making SLO claims directly.
open_questions: Do we price burst as included up to a fixed monthly allowance (e.g., X% of committed) or keep it as “included best-effort” with metered overages for Plus/Premium? Need alignment with metering implementation (ENG-19302).
How do we handle customers wanting multi-model deployments on one Dedicated pool? Does tier mapping require “dominant model class” constraints for pricing (e.g., Llama-70B vs 8B)?
Do we need separate shapes/prices for long-context heavy workloads (memory-bound) vs short-context high-QPS (compute-bound), or do we keep one shape and rely on sizing guidance + exclusions?
What’s the minimum catalog to launch with given regional supply constraints (H100 scarcity in EU)?
Should Premium include warm pool / spare node baked in by default, or offer as an add-on SKU?
comments: 2025-02-25 (Lauren Bishop): Need first pass of tier→shape mapping by end of next week so we can unblock PM-503 contract language. Please keep the catalog small and region-aware. Irene/Vanessa: can you confirm which shapes are “quoteable” in US/EU for March/April lead times?

2025-02-27 (Vanessa Ortiz): Supply note: H100-4x in EU is constrained through May; recommend we treat A100-8x as the Premium default in EU with H100-4x as ‘when available’. US-East can support limited H100-4x starting late March. L40S availability is good but perf variance is higher across vendors—need benchmark ranges in the sheet.

2025-03-01 (Rishi Malhotra): Ran initial unit econ sensitivity: Premium with too much reserved headroom can dip below 55% GM unless priced appropriately. Suggest we explicitly price the “premium operational posture” (spares/warm pool) rather than hiding it. OK with an add-on if Sales can quote it cleanly.

2025-03-04 (Isabelle Laurent): Guardrails need to be simple. Approval matrix is fine, but we should also define a small number of standard deal packages (12 mo / 24 mo) with pre-approved discounts so AEs aren’t constantly escalating. Also please define what qualifies as a “custom shape” (e.g., A100-6x) vs supported catalog.

2025-03-07 (Lauren Bishop): Action items: (1) Laura/Rishi to propose list price bands per shape with GM floors (internal only). (2) Vanessa to confirm region availability + lead times for the v1 catalog. (3) Lauren/Isabelle to finalize discount approvals + triggers. Target: circulate v1 doc for exec review by 3/12.
